learning_outcomes:
Major
Programme:
Upon
completion of the Programme,
Knowledge
and comprehension
Students
will have acquired the following knowledge:
(1)  |  Linear
Algebra and Abstract Algebra;
(2)  |  Analysis which includes
Calculus, Real Analysis, Complex Analysis, Fourier Analysis and Functional
Analysis;
(3)  |  Differential Geometry;
(4)  |  Computer programming for
Mathematics and Numerical Analysis.
Skills
and Generic Competencies
Students
will have acquired a set of generic competencies:
(1)  |  Ability to understand broad
mathematical literature independently;
(2)  |  Awareness of mathematical
problems arising in generic situations;
(3)  |  Ability to communicate
mathematical problems effectively;
(4)  |  Ability to formulate
mathematical problems and know how to find ways to solve them;
(5)  |  Ability to solve real-life
problems with mathematical software.
Professional
Skills
In
addition, students will have possessed professional skills in at least one of
the following sectors:
(1)  |  Graduate school research;
(2)  |  Teaching;
(3)  |  Interdisciplinary research
between mathematics and other scientific disciplines.
Value and attitudes
Upon
graduation, our students will be able to apply their mathematical knowledge
generically in their future profession in a way that is unique for
mathematically trained experts. They will be able to make important original
contributions in mathematical sciences and lead breakthrough of
interdisciplinary mathematical-science applications.

Explanatory
Notes:
1.  |  Students
enrolled in the Bachelor of Science Programme in Mathematical
Sciences/Mathematics and Applied Mathematics
jointly organized by CUHK and CUHK(SZ) (joint programme) should normally
spend four regular terms at CUHK(SZ) during the four years of study, except otherwise
specified in 2. below.
2.  |  Students who join term-time exchange programme must
spend at least three regular terms at
CUHK(SZ) during the four years of study.
3.  |  Students
enrolled in the joint programme can take substitute/equivalent/alternative
courses either at CUHK or CUHK(SZ). The list of substitute/equivalent/alternative
courses is available at this link (https://www.zsims.cuhk.edu.hk/en/). Students
should not take a course and its substitute/equivalent/alternative course. Should they do so, only one course will be counted
towards the fulfillment
of the unit requirements. Grades of relevant substitute/equivalent/alternative
courses taken at CUHK(SZ) will be transferred to CUHK for the purpose of calculation of
GPA, Major GPA and credit units.
4.  |  All Faculty Package courses,
Required Courses, and Elective Courses will be included in the
calculation of Major GPA for honors classification.
5.  |  A student who wishes to
transfer to the programmes offered by the Faculty of Science or Faculty
of Engineering shall follow the prevailing rules and regulations of the
University and obtain prior permission from the School Director through
written application. Such applications should be made one month before
the commencement of the University’s designated application period for
the change of programme. No such application shall be accepted once the
application period as announced by the University has commenced. In
general, students must apply for a change of programme no later than the
third year of attendance of their undergraduate studies.
6.  |  Students admitted by CUHK will
be conferred a Bachelor of Science degree in Mathematical Sciences upon
completion of all graduation requirements. Students may apply to pursue
Ph.D. study under the arrangements of the Articulated B.Sc. – Ph.D. Programme in Mathematical Sciences
(ABP), and they must declare the opt-in according to the stipulated
procedures by the beginning of the fourth year of attendance. Students
are required to obtain a Bachelor of Science degree with honours not
lower than Second Class and to satisfy the minimum admission requirements
prescribed by the Graduate School and Zhizhen School in order to be
eligible to proceed with postgraduate studies, subject to the prevailing
University regulations and approval by the relevant authorities.
Graduates from the Bachelor’s programmes from CUHK are deemed to have
fulfilled the University’s English Language requirements.
7.  |  Students who wish to pursue
Ph.D. study under the ABP should take note of the following:
(i)  |  For CUHK students who are
subsequently admitted to the Ph.D. of the ABP, the 5000-level courses
that they complete under this programme will be automatically recognized
to fulfill the coursework requirement for the Ph.D. Programme, subject to
prevailing guidelines. No application for course and unit
exemptions is required.
(ii)  |  In order to fulfill the
graduation requirements for postgraduate study, students must complete a
minimum of 9 months of non-local learning/research experience, with at
least 3 consecutive months of such experience. A formal term-time
exchange programme during undergraduate study, or non-consecutive and
substantial non-local learning/research experiences of 4 months or more
offered by the University, Colleges, the Faculty of Engineering or
Science, Zhizhen School, the Mathematics Department and other relevant
programmes may also be considered, subject to the approval of the
Division Head
